===XMPP===
{{Distinguish||text=[[XAMPP]], a web server software stack, or [[Extreme Memory Profile|Extreme Memory Profile (XMP)]], a memory overclocking standard}}
{{Short description|none}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=November 2019}}
'''Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol''' ('''XMPP''') is a [[communication protocol]] for [[message-oriented middleware]] based on [[XML]] (Extensible Markup Language).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gnomis.org/presentasjoner/oslo2005/xmpp.pdf |title=XMPP as MOM – Greater NOrdic MIddleware Symposium (GNOMIS) |first=Leif |last=Johansson |publisher=University of Stockholm |date=April 18, 2005 |place=Oslo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110510012207/http://www.gnomis.org/presentasjoner/oslo2005/xmpp.pdf |archive-date=May 10, 2011 }}</ref> It enables the near-real-time exchange of structured yet [[extensibility|extensible]] data between any two or more network entities.<ref>{{Cite IETF | title = Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP): Core | rfc = 6120 | last1 = Saint-Andre | first1 = P. |date=March 2011 | publisher = [[Internet Engineering Task Force|IETF]] | accessdate = May 4, 2014}}</ref> Originally named '''Jabber''',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cisco.com/web/about/ac49/ac0/ac1/ac258/JabberInc.html |title=Jabber Inc |publisher=Cisco.com |access-date=November 24, 2012}}</ref> the protocol was developed by the eponymous open-source community in 1999 for [[real-time computing|near real-time]] [[instant messaging]] (IM), [[presence information]], and [[contact list]] maintenance. Designed to be [[Extensibility|extensible]], the protocol has been used also for publish-subscribe systems, signalling for [[Voice over IP|VoIP]], video, [[file transfer]], [[Game|gaming]], the [[Internet of things|Internet of Things]] (IoT) applications such as the [[smart grid]], and [[social networking service]]s.

Unlike most instant messaging protocols, XMPP is defined in an [[open standard]] and uses an [[open system (computing)|open systems]] approach of development and application, by which anyone may implement an XMPP service and interoperate with other organizations' implementations. Because XMPP is an open protocol, implementations can be developed using any [[software license]] and many server, client, and library implementations are distributed as [[free and open-source software]]. Numerous [[freeware]] and [[commercial software]] implementations also exist.

The [[Internet Engineering Task Force]] (IETF) formed an XMPP [[working group]] in 2002 to formalize the core protocols as an IETF instant messaging and presence technology. The XMPP Working group produced four specifications (RFC 3920, RFC 3921, RFC 3922, RFC 3923), which were approved as Proposed Standards in 2004. In 2011, RFC 3920 and RFC 3921 were superseded by RFC 6120 and RFC 6121 respectively, with RFC 6122 specifying the XMPP address format. In 2015, RFC 6122 was superseded by RFC 7622. In addition to these core protocols standardized at the IETF, the [[XMPP Standards Foundation]] (formerly the Jabber Software Foundation) is active in developing open XMPP extensions.

XMPP-based software is deployed widely across the Internet, and by 2003, was used by over ten million people worldwide, according to the [[XMPP Standards Foundation]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://xmpp.org/xsf/press/2003-09-22.shtml |title=Jabber Instant Messaging User Base Surpasses ICQ |publisher=[[XMPP Standards Foundation]] |date=September 22, 2003 |access-date=November 30, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071103080257/http://www.xmpp.org/xsf/press/2003-09-22.shtml |archive-date=November 3, 2007 }}</ref>

{{IPstack}}

==SMS texting apps==
Below are apps that are used for texting via SMS. Generally, these apps offer  various features for expanded messaging, or group texts; however, all messages are received by others as regular SMS text messages.

===Textfree===

Textfree (formerly Pinger) is an application made by [[Pinger]] that allows users to text and call over the internet for free or for a price. The application runs on [[iOS]],<ref>[http://www.apppicker.com/app-review/textfree-pinger-text-free-call-free-worldwide-messenger-top-100-app-reviews/ Textfree is now Pinger App Review]{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, AppPicker</ref> [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[Microsoft Windows]] and [[Macintosh]] devices. Competitors include GOGII, Optini and [[WhatsApp]].

==Stand-alone messaging platforms==
Below are stand-alone apps that are generally focused upon instant messaging as their core feature; however, almost all of these also include numerous distinct additional features such as group chats, video calls, emojis, etc.

These apps do not use SMS messaging; rather, users of this app receive messages through the app interface, not through SMS texting.

===Dingtone===
Dingtone is an application made by Dingtone that allows users to text and call over the internet for free or for a price. The application runs on [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[IOS]], [[Microsoft Windows]] and [[Macintosh]] devices.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dingtone Desktop App for Mac and PC {{!}} Manage Multiple Dingtone Accounts |url=https://webcatalog.io/apps/dingtone/ |website=WebCatalog |access-date=9 January 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

===Google Voice===
[[Google Voice]] is a [[telephone]] service that provides [[call forwarding]] and [[voicemail]] services, voice and text messaging.

Google Voice provides a U.S. telephone number, chosen by the user from available numbers in selected area codes, free of charge to each user account. Calls to this number are forwarded to telephone numbers that each user must configure in the account web portal. Multiple destinations may be specified that ring simultaneously for incoming calls. Service establishment requires a United States telephone number. A user may answer and receive calls on any of the ringing phones as configured in the [[web portal]]. During a received call the user may switch between the configured telephones.<ref name="pogue2"/>

Users {{As of|2010|12|alt=in the U.S.}} may place outbound calls to domestic and international destinations. Calls may be initiated from any of the configured telephones, as well as from a mobile device app, or from the account portal.<ref name="pogue2">{{cite news|last=Pogue|first=David|title=One Number to Ring Them All|work=The New York Times|date=March 11, 2009|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/03/12/technology/personaltech/12pogue.html}}</ref> As of August 2011, users in many other countries also may place outbound calls from the web-based application to domestic and international phone numbers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Google Voice Blog|date=August 2, 2011|url=http://googlevoiceblog.blogspot.com/2011/08/calling-from-gmail-now-in-38-languages.html|access-date=August 4, 2011|quote=Calling from Gmail now in 38 languages, with lower rates to over 150 destinations.}}</ref>

Many other Google Voice services—such as [[voicemail]], free text messaging, call history, [[call screening]], blocking of unwanted calls, and [[speech recognition|voice transcription]] to text of voicemail messages—are also available to {{As of|2010|12|alt=U.S. residents}}.<ref>{{cite web
|title= Google Voice
|url= https://www.google.com/googlevoice/about.html
|access-date= August 21, 2009}}</ref> In terms of product integration, transcribed and audio voicemails, missed call notifications, and/or text messages can optionally be forwarded to an email account of the user's choice. Additionally, text messages can be sent and received via the familiar email or IM interface by reading and writing text messages in numbers in [[Google Talk]] respectively (PC-to-Phone texting). Google Voice multi-way videoconferencing (with support for document sharing) is now integrated with [[Google]] Hangouts.<ref>{{cite web |title= Google+ Hangouts (Videoconferencing) |url= https://www.google.com/+/learnmore/hangouts/ |access-date= July 16, 2012}}</ref>

The service is configured and maintained by the user in a web-based application, styled after Google's e-mail service, [[Gmail]], or with Android and iOS apps on smart phones or tablets. Google Voice {{As of|2010|12|alt=currently}} provides free PC-to-phone calling within the United States and Canada, and PC-to-PC voice and video calling worldwide between users of the Google+ Hangouts browser plugin (available for Windows, Intel-based Mac OS X, and Linux).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.google.com/chat/video |title=Google voice and video chat |access-date=January 3, 2010}}</ref>

===GroupMe===
[[GroupMe]] works by downloading the [[Mobile app|app]] or accessing the service online, and then forming an account by providing your name, cell phone number and a password, or you can connect through your [[Facebook]] or [[Twitter]] account.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://groupme.com/|title=GroupMe – Group text messaging with GroupMe}}</ref> The service then syncs with your contacts and from that point forward the user can make groups, limited to 500 members. An individual who is part of an active group has the ability to turn off notifications for the app; users will still receive the message, but will not be notified about it. Each group is given a label and assigned a unique number. Some of the features of the app include the ability to share photos, videos, locations, create events, and [[emojis]] from various packs.

GroupMe has a web client as well as apps for [[iOS]], [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[Windows Phone]], and [[Windows 10]].
Those who do not wish to use the app can still send and receive GroupMe messages through [[Short Message Service|SMS]] (only available in the United States).<ref>{{cite web|title=Do I need a smartphone to use GroupMe?|url=http://help.groupme.com/hc/en-us/articles/217104147|access-date=2020-08-06|website=GroupMe Support|language=en-US}}</ref>
Users begin by creating a "group" and adding contacts. When someone sends a message, everyone in the group can see and respond to it. The app allows users to easily attach and send pictures, documents, videos and web-links as well. Users can also send private messages, but only to users who are also active on the GroupMe app.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jacobsson |first=Sarah |url=http://www.pcworld.com/article/250439/groupme_app_review_perfect_for_coordinating_with_friends.html |title=GroupMe App Review: Perfect for Coordinating With Friends &#124; TechHive |publisher=Pcworld.com |date=2012-02-26 |access-date=2013-07-08}}</ref>

GroupMe has been used as a means for studying the usage of messaging clients in educational settings. Use cases include facilitating online course discussions, small group work, and other course communications for both in-person and online sections.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gronseth|first1=Susie|last2=Hebert|first2=Waneta|date=2019-01-01|title=GroupMe: Investigating Use of Mobile Instant Messaging in Higher Education Courses|journal=TechTrends|language=en|volume=63|issue=1|pages=15–22|doi=10.1007/s11528-018-0361-y|s2cid=69857201|issn=1559-7075}}</ref> Though unconventional, using GroupMe to facilitate discussion in an environment where students already interact has been found to encourage rhetorical thinking and overall engagement. Researchers have found alternatives for literacy learning as a "legitimate academic genre", given a student population that communicates in a variety of modes. Research around GroupMe furthers the argument that computer-mediated communication is a valuable space for learning in an increasingly globalized society.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Quang|first=Ly|date=Spring 2020|title=The Case for GroupMe: Rhetorical Thinking Thrives Among Students Using App|url=http://www.literacyandtechnology.org/uploads/1/3/6/8/136889/jlt_v21_1_ly.pdf|journal=Journal of Literacy and Technology|volume=21|issue=1: Spring / Summer 2020|archive-date=July 12, 2020|access-date=December 10, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200712013335/http://www.literacyandtechnology.org/uploads/1/3/6/8/136889/jlt_v21_1_ly.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===KakaoTalk===
[[KakaoTalk]], commonly referred to as "KaTalk" in South Korea, is a free mobile [[instant messaging]] [[Application software|application]] for [[smartphone]]s with free text and free call features, operated by [[Kakao]] Corporation. It was launched on March 18, 2010, and is currently available on [[iOS]], [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[Bada OS]], [[BlackBerry]], [[Windows Phone]], [[Nokia Asha]], [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] and [[macOS]].

As of May 2017, KakaoTalk had 220 million registered and 49 million [[monthly active users]]. It is available in 15 languages.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/kakaotalk/id362057947?mt=8|title=KakaoTalk on the App Store|website=App Store|language=en-US|access-date=2018-04-19}}</ref> The app is also used by 93% of smartphone owners in [[South Korea]], where it is the number one messaging app.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.trutower.com/2013/12/23/kakao-number-of-users-revenues-and-profits-2013/ |title=KakaoTalk on 93 Percent of Smartphones in South Korea, Expecting $200 Million in Revenue – TruTower |access-date=December 10, 2020 |archive-date=August 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806104943/https://www.trutower.com/2013/12/23/kakao-number-of-users-revenues-and-profits-2013/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In addition to free calls and messages,  users can share photos, videos, voice messages, location, URL links as well as contact information. Both one-on-one and group chats are available over [[Wi-Fi]], [[3G]] or [[LTE (telecommunication)|LTE]], and there are no limits to the number of people on a group chat.

Airlines such as Southwest which allow free WhatsApp in flight also have functionality for KaTalk, even though their literature omits to mention same.

The app automatically synchronizes the user's contact list on their smartphones with the contact list on the app to find friends who are on the service. Users can also search for friends by KakaoTalk ID without having to know their phone numbers. The KakaoTalk service also allows its users to export their messages and save them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.trutower.com/kakaotalk/|title=KakaoTalk TruTower|date=2013-02-06|access-date=2013-02-06}}</ref>

KakaoTalk began as a [[Instant messenger|messenger service]] but has become a platform for the distribution of various third-party content and apps, including hundreds of games, which users can download and play with their friends through the messaging platform.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thenextweb.com/asia/2013/07/16/korean-messaging-app-kakao-talks-games-platform-grossed-311-million-in-h1-2013/|title=Korean messaging app Kakao Talk's games platform grossed $311 million in H1 2013|date=2013-07-16|access-date=2014-04-23}}</ref> Through the "Plus Friend" feature, users can follow brands, media and celebrities to receive exclusive messages, coupons and other real-time information through KakaoTalk chatrooms. Users can also purchase real-life goods through the messenger's "Gifting" platform.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://online.wsj.com/news/articles/SB10001424052702304834704579405232330645204|title=South Korea's Kakao Pushes Boundaries of Social Media|newspaper=Wall Street Journal|date=2014-02-26|access-date=2014-04-21|last1=Cheng|first1=Jonathan}}</ref>

Besides those listed above, the app has these additional features:

* VoiceTalk, free calls and conference calls (with support for up to five people) 
* Photo, video, location, and contact information sharing
* Polling and scheduling feature for members in the chatroom
* [[K-pop]] & Local Star Friends (Plus Friends)
* Walkie-talkie
* Customizable themes (for iOS and Android)
* Game platform
* Stickers and animated emoticons
*Plus Mate: You can add your favorite brand, star, or media as your friend to receive a variety of content and benefits.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kakaocorp.com/service/KakaoTalk?lang=ko|title=카카오톡|website=kakaocorp.com|language=ko|access-date=2019-03-17}}</ref>

===Kik Messenger===
Kik Messenger, commonly called Kik, is a [[freeware]] [[instant messaging]] [[mobile app]] from the [[Canada|Canadian]] company Kik Interactive, available free of charge on [[iOS]] and [[Android (operating system)|Android]] operating systems.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kikinteractive.zendesk.com/entries/23499123-How-do-I-get-the-Kik-app-|title=How do I get the Kik app|access-date=2014-02-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221220357/https://kikinteractive.zendesk.com/entries/23499123-How-do-I-get-the-Kik-app-|archive-date=2014-02-21|url-status=dead}}</ref> It uses a [[smartphone]]'s data plan or [[Wi-Fi]] to transmit and receive messages, photos, videos, sketches, mobile web pages, and other content after users register a username.<ref>{{cite web|title=Is Kik Free?|url=https://kikinteractive.zendesk.com/entries/23485821-Is-Kik-free-|access-date=2014-02-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141108065505/https://kikinteractive.zendesk.com/entries/23485821-Is-Kik-free-|archive-date=2014-11-08|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kik is known for its features preserving users' anonymity, such as allowing users to register without the need to provide a telephone number or valid email address. However, the application does not employ [[end-to-end encryption]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Wagner|first=Kurt|date=2015-12-21|title=Is Your Messaging App Encrypted?|url=https://www.vox.com/2015/12/21/11621610/is-your-messaging-app-encrypted|access-date=2020-10-08|website=Vox|language=en}}</ref> and the company also logs user [[IP address]]es, which could be used to determine the user's [[Internet service provider|ISP]] and approximate location.<ref name="dingman">{{cite news |last=Dingman |first=Shane |date=2015-03-16 |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/technology/for-fast-growing-chat-apps-child-predators-are-a-pervasive-threat/article23485785/ |title=For Fast-Growing Chat Apps Like Waterloo's Kik, Child Exploitation a Pervasive Threat|newspaper=[[The Globe and Mail]] |location=[[Toronto]], [[Ontario]]| url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150317060634/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/technology/for-fast-growing-chat-apps-child-predators-are-a-pervasive-threat/article23485785/ |archive-date=2015-03-17 | access-date=2016-02-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.kik.com/assets/Uploads/LEO1-1-Kik-s-Guide-for-Law-Enforcement-September-2016.pdf | title = Kik's Guide for Law Enforcement | work = Kik Messenger | access-date = 2017-01-11 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170113162319/https://www.kik.com/assets/Uploads/LEO1-1-Kik-s-Guide-for-Law-Enforcement-September-2016.pdf | archive-date = 2017-01-13 | url-status = dead }}</ref> This information, as well as "reported" conversations are regularly surrendered upon request by law enforcement organizations,<ref>{{cite web|date=2020-10-08|title=Law Enforcement Guide – Law Enforcement Resource Center|url=https://lawenforcement.kik.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039841472-Law-Enforcement-Guide|access-date=2020-10-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201008094040/https://lawenforcement.kik.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039841472-Law-Enforcement-Guide|archive-date=2020-10-08}}</ref> sometimes without the need for a [[court order]].<ref>{{cite web|date=2020-10-08|title=Download our Emergency Disclosure Request Form – Law Enforcement Resource Center|url=https://lawenforcement.kik.com/hc/en-us/articles/203421499-Download-our-Emergency-Disclosure-Request-Form|access-date=2020-10-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201008093510/https://lawenforcement.kik.com/hc/en-us/articles/203421499-Download-our-Emergency-Disclosure-Request-Form|archive-date=2020-10-08}}</ref>

Kik was originally intended to be a music-sharing app<ref>{{cite web|date=2009-11-22|url=http://www.kik.com/kik_fact_sheet_nov9.pdf|access-date=2020-10-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091122133517/http://www.kik.com/kik_fact_sheet_nov9.pdf|archive-date=2009-11-22}}</ref> before transitioning to messaging, briefly offering users the ability to send a limited number of [[SMS]] text messages directly from the application.<ref>{{cite web|date=2010-05-13|title=Kik {{!}} Text Anyone for Free|url=http://kik.com/|access-date=2020-10-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513001148/http://kik.com/|archive-date=2010-05-13}}</ref>  During the first 15 days after Kik's re-release as a [[Messaging apps|messaging app]], over 1 million accounts were created.<ref>{{cite web|date=2010-11-15|title=Kik Interactive {{!}} Crazy Start-Up World|url=http://www.kik.com/blog/|access-date=2020-10-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101115121825/http://www.kik.com/blog/|archive-date=2010-11-15}}</ref>  In May 2016, Kik Messenger announced that they had approximately 300 million registered users, and was used by approximately 40% of United States' teenagers.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://techcrunch.com/2016/05/11/kik-already-has-over-6000-bots-reaching-300-million-registered-users/ | title = Kik already has over 6,000 bots reaching 300 million registered users | work = Tech Crunch | date = 11 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Kik adds senior vice president of engineering to scale engineering and product teams|url=https://www.kik.com/blog/kik-adds-senior-vice-president-of-engineering-to-scale-engineering-and-product-t/|access-date=2020-10-08|website=www.kik.com|language=en|archive-date=December 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201229015912/https://www.kik.com/blog/kik-adds-senior-vice-president-of-engineering-to-scale-engineering-and-product-t/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Kik Messenger announced in October 2019 they had signed a letter of intent with MediaLab AI, followed by the announcement Kik Interactive would be reducing their staff from 100 to just 19.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/10/13/kik-says-its-here-to-stay-following-shutdown-reports/|title=Kik says it's 'here to stay,' following shutdown reports|newspaper=Techcrunch|access-date=December 17, 2020|archive-date=October 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013194953/https://techcrunch.com/2019/10/13/kik-says-its-here-to-stay-following-shutdown-reports/|url-status=live}}</ref>  MediaLab owns several [[mobile app]]s, most notably [[Whisper (app)|Whisper]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kik is here to stay!|url=https://www.kik.com/blog/kik-medialab-acquisition/|access-date=2020-10-08|website=www.kik.com|language=en|archive-date=December 16, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201216181827/https://www.kik.com/blog/kik-medialab-acquisition/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

A main attraction of Kik that differentiates it from other messaging apps is its anonymity. To register for the Kik service, a user must enter a first and last name, e-mail address, and birth date (which must show that the user is at least 13 years old<ref name=kiksafetyguide020416>{{cite web |url=http://blog.kik.com/2016/02/04/kiks-safety-guide-for-parents/ |title=Kik's Safety Guide for Parents |date=2016-02-04 |website=kik.com |publisher=Kik Interactive |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160213194432/http://blog.kik.com/2016/02/04/kiks-safety-guide-for-parents/ |archive-date=2016-02-13 |access-date=2016-02-13 |quote=If the birthday entered is for someone younger than 13, the account won’t be registered.}}</ref>), and select a username. The Kik registration process does not request or require the entry of a phone number (although the user has the option to enter one<ref name=kiksafetyguide020416/>), unlike some other messaging services that require a user to provide a functioning mobile phone number.<ref name=dingman/>

''[[The New York Times]]'' has reported that, according to law enforcement, Kik's anonymity features go beyond those of most widely used apps.<ref name="stolberg">{{cite news |last1=Stolberg |first1=Sheryl Gay |last2=Pérez-Peña |first2=Richard | date=2016-02-05 |title=Wildly Popular App Kik Offers Teenagers, and Predators, Anonymity |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/02/06/us/social-media-apps-anonymous-kik-crime.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |location=[[New York City]] |access-date=2016-02-13 }}</ref> As of February 2016, Kik's guide for law enforcement said that the company cannot locate user accounts based on first and last name, e-mail address and/or birth date; the exact username is required to locate a particular account. The guide further said that the company does not have access to content or "historical user data" such as photographs, videos, and the text of conversations, and that photographs and videos are automatically deleted shortly after they are sent. A limited amount of data from a particular account (identified by exact username), including first and last name, birth date, e-mail address, link to a current profile picture, device-related information, and user location information such as the most recently used [[IP address]], can be preserved for a period of 90 days pending receipt of a valid order from law enforcement. Kik's anonymity has also been cited as a protective safety measure for good faith users, in that "users have screennames; the app doesn't share phone numbers or email addresses."<ref name=connectsafely>{{cite web |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> | date=2014-05-20 |url=http://www.connectsafely.org/kik-messengers-smart-new-safety-features/ |title=Kik Messenger's Smart New Safety Features |website=ConnectSafely.org | publisher=Connect Safely: Smart Socializing Starts Here | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150520010107/http://www.connectsafely.org/kik-messengers-smart-new-safety-features |archive-date=2015-05-20 | access-date=2016-02-13 }}</ref>

Kik introduced several new user features in 2015, including a full-screen in-chat browser that allows users to find and share content from the web;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/04/14/kik-full-browser/#.hbxhvu:qsVF/ |title=Kik Introduces An In-Chat Browser For Its Mobile Messaging App|date=April 14, 2015 |publisher=TechCrunch}}</ref> a feature allowing users to send previously recorded videos in Kik Messenger for Android and iOS; and "Kik Codes", which assigns each user a unique code similar to a [[QR code]], making it easier to connect and chat with other users.<ref>{{cite web|title = Kik Codes launch on Kik Messenger, making it easier to connect with people {{!}} TruTower|url = http://www.trutower.com/2015/09/08/kik-codes-available-ios-android-39248/|website = TruTower|date = September 8, 2015|access-date = 2015-12-17|language = en-us}}</ref> Kik joined the [[Virtual Global Taskforce]], a global anti-child-abuse organization, in March 2015.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2015-03-10/kik-adds-tools-to-prevent-child-exploitation-on-messaging-app|title=Kik Adds Tools to Prevent Child Exploitation on Messaging App|date=March 10, 2015|first=Sarah|last=Frier|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|publisher=Bloomberg}}</ref> Kik began using Microsoft's [[PhotoDNA]] in March 2015 to premoderate images added by users.<ref name="dingman" /> That same month, Kik released native video capture allowing users to record up to 15 seconds in the chat window.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/03/04/kik-native-video-capture/|title=Chat App Kik Adds Native Video In Step Towards More Interactive Content|first=Jon|last=Russell|date=March 4, 2015|publisher=Tech Crunch}}</ref> In October 2015, Kik partnered with the [[Ad Council]] as part of an anti-bullying campaign. The campaign was featured on the app and Kik released stickers in collaboration with the campaign.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://digiday.com/brands/adobe-gsp-ad-council-introduce-eye-emoji-new-anti-bullying-campaign/|title=Adobe, GS&P and Ad Council introduce eye emoji for new anti-bullying campaign|first=Tanya|last=Dua|date=October 22, 2015|magazine=[[Digiday]]}}</ref> Kik released a feature to send GIFs as emojis in November 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/11/16/chat-app-kiks-newest-feature-makes-sending-gifs-as-easy-as-emoji/|title=Chat App Kik's Newest Feature Makes Sending GIFs As Easy As Emoji|date=November 16, 2015|first=Jon|last=Russell|publisher=Tech Crunch}}</ref> Kik added SafePhoto to its safety features in October 2016 which "detects, reports, and deletes known child exploitation images" sent through the platform. Kik partnered with ConnectSafely in 2016 to produce a "parents handbook" and joined The Technology Coalition, an anti-sexual exploitation group including [[Facebook]], [[Google]], [[Twitter]] and [[LinkedIn]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://venturebeat.com/2016/10/13/kik-steps-up-efforts-to-keep-teen-users-safe/|title=Kik steps up efforts to keep teen users safe|first=Khari|last=Johnson|date=October 13, 2016|publisher=Venture Beat|access-date=December 17, 2020|archive-date=August 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812042810/https://venturebeat.com/2016/10/13/kik-steps-up-efforts-to-keep-teen-users-safe/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Line===
[[Line (software)|Line]] (styled in all caps as '''LINE''') is a [[freeware]] app for [[instant messaging|instant communications]] on [[Electronics|electronic devices]] such as [[smartphone]]s, [[tablet computer]]s, and [[personal computer]]s. Line users exchange [[text message|texts]], [[computer graphics|images]], video and audio, and conduct free [[Voice over IP|VoIP]] conversations and video conferences. In addition, Line is a platform providing various services including [[digital wallet]] as Line Pay, [[news]] stream as Line Today, [[video on demand]] as Line TV, and digital [[comic]] distribution as Line Manga and Line Webtoon. The service is operated by [[Line Corporation]], a [[Tokyo]]-based subsidiary of [[South Korea]]n internet search engine company [[Naver Corporation]].

Line is an application that works on multiple platforms and has access via multiple personal computers (Windows or macOS). The application will also give an option of address book syncing. This application also has a feature to add friends through the use of QR codes, by Line ID, and by shaking phones simultaneously. The application has a direct pop-out message box for reading and replying to make it easy for users to communicate. It also can share photos, videos and music with other users, send the current or any specific location, voice audio, emojis, stickers and emoticons to friends. Users can see a real-time confirmation when messages are sent and received or use a hidden chat feature, which can hide and delete a chat history (from both involved devices and Line servers) after a time set by the user.<ref name="Hidden Chats">{{cite web |url=https://thenextweb.com/apps/2014/07/22/messaging-app-line-gets-serious-privacy-telegram-inspired-hidden-chat-feature/ |title=Messaging app Line gets serious about privacy with Telegram-inspired 'hidden chat' feature |first=Jon|last=Russel |date=22 July 2014 |publisher=TheNextWeb |access-date=24 November 2014 }}</ref> The application also makes free voice and video calls.

Users can also chat and share media in a group by creating and joining groups that have up to 500 people. Chats also provide bulletin boards on which users can post, like, and comment. This application also has timeline and homepage features that allow users to post pictures, text and stickers on their homepages. Users can also change their Line theme to the theme Line provides in the theme shop for free or users can buy other famous cartoon characters they like. Line also has a feature, called a Snap movie, that users can use to record a stop-motion video and add in provided background music.

In January 2015, ''Line Taxi'' was released in Tokyo as a competitor to [[Uber]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vincent|first1=James|title=Japanese messaging app Line has launched a taxi service in Tokyo|url=https://www.theverge.com/2015/1/8/7513161/line-taxi-launches-in-japan-to-battle-Uber|access-date=3 September 2015|work=The Verge|date=8 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Cohen|first1=Dave|title=Line Taxi launches, gives Uber first major challenger in Japan|url=https://www.techinasia.com/line-taxi-launch/|access-date=3 September 2015|work=Tech In Asia|date=6 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Kosoff|first1=Maya|title=This Japanese Messaging App Is Launching Its Own Taxi Service To Take On Uber|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/line-messaging-app-taxi-service-2015-1|access-date=3 September 2015|work=Business Insider|date=8 January 2015}}</ref> Line launched a new android app called "Popcorn buzz" in June 2015. The app facilitates group calls with up to 200 members.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://previewtech.net/popcorn-buzz-app-line/|title=Popcorn Buzz app launched by Line. Can do group call|date=June 5, 2015|access-date=December 10, 2020|archive-date=October 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018184009/https://previewtech.net/popcorn-buzz-app-line/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In June a new Emoji keyboard was also released for iOS devices, which provides a Line-like experience with the possibility to add stickers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/06/17/you-wont-use-our-messaging-app-so-heres-a-funky-keyboard/|title=Line Takes Aims At The U.S. Market With An Emoji Keyboard App For iOS|first=Jon|last=Russell|date=June 17, 2015 }}</ref> In September 2015 a new Android launcher was released on the Play Store, helping the company to promote its own services through the new user interface.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2015/08/31/messaging-firm-line-introduces-a-launcher-app-for-android-devices/|title=Messaging Firm Line Introduces A Launcher App For Android Devices|first=Jon|last=Russell|date=September 2015 }}</ref>

===Signal===
[[Signal (messaging app)|Signal]] is a [[Cross-platform software|cross-platform]] [[encryption|encrypted]] [[messaging app|messaging service]] developed by the [[Signal Foundation]] and [[Signal Messenger LLC]]. It uses the Internet to send one-to-one and group messages, which can include files, voice notes, images and videos.<ref name="arbitrary-file-types">{{cite tweet |user=signalapp |number=859125874901135360 |date=1 May 2017 |title= Today's Signal release for Android, iOS, and Desktop includes the ability to send arbitrary file types.|accessdate=5 November 2018 }}</ref> It can also be used to make one-to-one voice and video calls, and the Android version can optionally function as an SMS app.<ref name="Mott-2017-03-14">{{cite web|last1=Mott|first1=Nathaniel|title=Signal's Encrypted Video Calling For iOS, Android Leaves Beta|url=http://www.tomshardware.com/news/signal-encrypted-video-calling-ios-android,33898.html|website=Tom's Hardware|publisher=Purch Group, Inc.|date=14 March 2017|access-date=14 March 2017}}</ref> <!---- <ref name="desktop-v1.35.1"/><ref name="Frosch 2016"/> ---->

Signal uses standard cellular [[telephone number]]s as identifiers and secures all communications to other Signal users with [[end-to-end encryption]]. The apps include mechanisms by which users can independently verify the identity of their contacts and the integrity of the data channel. <!----<ref name="Frosch 2016"/><ref name="Schröder-2016"/> --->

===Snapchat===

Snapchat sends messages referred to as "snaps"; snaps can consist of a photo or a short video, and can be edited to include filters and effects, text captions, and drawings.<ref name="pocketlint-7tips">{{cite web|title=7 Snapchat tips and tricks you probably had no clue about|url=http://www.pocket-lint.com/news/132491-7-snapchat-tips-and-tricks-you-probably-had-no-clue-about|website=Pocket-lint|access-date=December 19, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Snapchat Hands-on: Send Photos Set to Self-Destruct|url=http://blog.laptopmag.com/hands-on-with-snapchat-send-photos-set-to-self-destruct|work=Laptop|publisher=TechMedia Network|access-date=September 15, 2013|last=Alba|first=Davey|author-link=Davey Alba |date=May 16, 2012}}</ref> Snaps can be directed privately to selected contacts, or to a semi-public "Story" or a public "Story" called "Our Story."<ref name="tc-stories">{{cite web |first=Darrell |last=Etherington |title=Snapchat Gets Its Own Timeline With Snapchat Stories, 24-Hour Photo & Video Tales |url=https://techcrunch.com/2013/10/03/snapchat-gets-its-own-timeline-with-snapchat-stories-24-hour-photo-video-tales/ |website=[[TechCrunch]] |publisher=[[AOL]] |date=October 3, 2013 |access-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref> The ability to send video snaps was added as a feature option in December 2012. By holding down on the photo button while inside the app, a video of up to ten seconds in length can be captured. Spiegel explained that this process allowed the video data to be compressed into the size of a photo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jjcolao/2012/12/14/snapchat-adds-video-now-seeing-50-million-photos-a-day/|title=Snapchat Adds Video, Now Seeing 50 Million Photos A Day|last=Colao|first=J.J.|date=December 14, 2012|website=[[Forbes]]|access-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref>  A later update allowed the ability to record up to 60 seconds, but are still segmented into 10 second intervals. After a single viewing, the video disappears by default. On May 1, 2014, the ability to communicate via [[Videotelephony|video chat]] was added. Direct messaging features were also included in the update, allowing users to send [[ephemerality|ephemeral]] text messages to friends and family while saving any needed information by clicking on it.<ref name="verge-snapchatchat">{{cite web |first=Ellis |last=Hamburger |title=Real talk: the new Snapchat brilliantly mixes video and texting |url=https://www.theverge.com/2014/5/1/5670260/real-talk-the-new-snapchat-makes-texting-fun-again-video-calls |website=[[The Verge]] |publisher=[[Vox Media]] |date=May 1, 2014 |access-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Romain |last=Dillet |title=Snapchat Adds Ephemeral Text Chat And Video Calls |url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/05/01/snapchat-adds-text-chat-and-video-calls/ |website=[[TechCrunch]] |publisher=[[AOL]] |date=May 1, 2014 |access-date=April 27, 2017}}</ref> According to CIO, Snapchat uses real-time marketing concepts and temporality to make the app appealing to users.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cio.com/article/3043043/marketing/why-snapchat-is-the-next-big-thing-in-digital-marketing.html|title=Why Snapchat is the next big thing in digital marketing|website=CIO|date=March 11, 2016|publisher=Matt Kapko|access-date=March 17, 2018|archive-date=November 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106235552/https://www.cio.com/article/3043043/marketing/why-snapchat-is-the-next-big-thing-in-digital-marketing.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> According to Marketing Pro, Snapchat attracts interest and potential customers by combining the [[AIDA (marketing)]] model with modern digital technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marketingprofs.com/opinions/2015/27431/attention-interest-desire-action-using-aida-for-social-media|title=Attention, Interest, Desire, Action: Using AIDA for Social Media|website=MarketingProfs|publisher=Sarah Green|access-date=March 17, 2018}}</ref>

Private message photo snaps can be viewed for a user-specified length of time (1 to 10 seconds as determined by the sender) before they become inaccessible. Users were previously required to hold down on the screen in order to view a snap; this behavior was removed in July 2015<ref name="verge-nomoreholding">{{cite web |first=Sam |last=Sheffer |title=Snapchat is changing the way you watch snaps and add friends |url=https://www.theverge.com/2015/7/1/8861131/snapchat-update-2015-tap-to-play-story |website=[[The Verge]] |publisher=[[Vox Media]] |date=July 1, 2015 |access-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref> The requirement to hold on the screen was intended to frustrate the ability to take [[screenshot]]s of snaps; the Snapchat app does not prevent screenshots from being taken but can notify the sender if it detects that it has been saved. However, these notifications can be bypassed through either unauthorized modifications to the app or by obtaining the image through external means.<ref name="Forbes, touch">{{cite web |first=J.J. |last=Colao |title=Snapchat: The Biggest No-Revenue Mobile App Since Instagram |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jjcolao/2012/11/27/snapchat-the-biggest-no-revenue-mobile-app-since-instagram/ |website=[[Forbes]] |date=November 27, 2012 |access-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref><ref name="TC, billion snaps">{{cite web |first=Billy |last=Gallagher |title=You Know What's Cool? A Billion Snapchats: App Sees Over 20 Million Photos Shared Per Day, Releases On Android |url=https://techcrunch.com/2012/10/29/billion-snapchats/ |website=[[TechCrunch]] |publisher=[[AOL]] |date=October 29, 2012 |access-date=April 10, 2017}}</ref><ref name="All Things, text overlay">{{cite news|title=Fast-Growing Photo-Messaging App Snapchat Launches on Android|url=http://allthingsd.com/20121029/fast-growing-photo-messaging-app-snapchat-launches-on-android/|access-date=December 22, 2012|newspaper=All Things D|date=October 29, 2012|last=Gannes|first=Liz }}</ref> One snap per day can be replayed for free.<ref name="wired-replay"/> In September 2015, Snapchat introduced the option to purchase additional replays through [[Microtransaction|in-app purchases]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Lauren |last=Hockenson |title=Snapchat Replay? You can now pay Snapchat to replay snaps! |url=https://thenextweb.com/apps/2015/09/15/snapchats-latest-update-brings-selfie-lenses-paid-replays/ |website=The Next Web |date=September 15, 2015 |access-date=May 4, 2017}}</ref><ref name="wired-replay">{{cite journal |first=Brian |last=Barrett |title=Snapchat Now Charges if You Want to Replay Snaps |url=https://www.wired.com/2015/09/snapchat-replay-paid |journal=[[Wired (website)|Wired]]  |date=September 15, 2015 |access-date=May 4, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Sean |last=O'Kane |title=Snapchat now lets you pay to replay snaps |url=https://www.theverge.com/2015/9/15/9330955/snapchat-replay-snaps-paid-in-app |website=[[The Verge]] |publisher=[[Vox Media]] |date=September 15, 2015 |access-date=May 4, 2017}}</ref> The ability to purchase extra replays was removed in April 2016.<ref>{{cite web |first=Alex |last=Heath |title=Snapchat quietly made a big change to the way messages expire |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/snapchat-lets-you-reply-to-every-snap-once-2016-4 |website=[[Business Insider]] |publisher=[[Axel Springer SE]] |date=April 22, 2016 |access-date=May 4, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |first=Jordan |last=Valinsky |title=Snapchat quietly kills in-app purchase option |url=https://digiday.com/media/snapchat-shelves-snap-replays/ |magazine=[[Digiday]] |date=April 22, 2016 |access-date=May 4, 2017}}</ref>

Friends can be added via usernames and phone contacts, using customizable "[[Aztec Code|Snapcodes]]," or through the "Add Nearby" function, which scans for users near their location who are also in the Add Nearby menu.<ref name="verge-nomoreholding"/><ref name="whatshouldmarketers">{{cite web|title=What marketers should know about Snapchat|url=http://www.brandrepublic.com/news/1186152/sexting-branding-marketers-know-snapchat-nickykc/|work=Brand Republic|publisher=[[Haymarket Media Group]]|access-date=July 21, 2013|last=Kemp| first=Nicola |date=June 13, 2013}}</ref> Spiegel explained that Snapchat is intended to counteract the trend of users being compelled to manage an idealized [[online identity]] of themselves, which he says has "taken all of the fun out of communicating."<ref name="Forbes, touch" />

===Tango===

Tango is a third-party,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gottabemobile.com/2013/03/20/american-law-enforcement-wants-carriers-to-save-your-incriminating-text- |title=American law enforcement wants carriers to save your incriminating text messages |last=Nguyen |first=Chuong |date=March 20, 2013 |access-date=May 14, 2013}}</ref> [[cross platform]] messaging [[application software]]<ref name="Pariseau">{{cite web |url= http://searchcloudcomputing.techtarget.com/news/2240179690/Private-cloud-to-public-cloud-migration-gets-easier-but-obstacles-remain |title=Private cloud to public cloud migration gets easier, but obstacles remain |last= Pariseau |first= Beth |date=March 15, 2013 |access-date=May 14, 2013}}</ref> for [[smartphones]] developed by TangoME, Inc.<ref name="Pariseau"/> in 2009. The app is free and began as one of the first provider of video calls, voice calls, texting, photo sharing, and games on a 3G network.<ref name="Pariseau" /><ref name="Fitchard">{{cite web|url=http://gigaom.com/2013/03/19/textme-tries-to-recreate-skype-as-a-mobile-first-app/|title=TextMe tries to recreate Skype as a mobile-first app|last=Fitchard|first=Kevin|date=March 19, 2013|access-date=May 14, 2013|archive-date=August 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812122154/https://gigaom.com/2013/03/19/textme-tries-to-recreate-skype-as-a-mobile-first-app/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Dredge" /><ref name="Moscaritolo" />

As of 2018, Tango has more than 400 million registered users.<ref name="Perez2">{{cite web|url=https://expandedramblings.com/index.php/tango-facts-statistics/|title=12 Tango Facts and Statistics (2020)By the Numbers|last=Smith|first=Craig|date=July 1, 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130524045035/http://www.thefullsignal.com/products/13846/tango-app-hits-100-million-users-launches-ipad-app|archive-date=May 24, 2013|access-date=May 14, 2013|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="Loeb">{{cite web|url=http://vator.tv/news/2013-03-14-asian-messaging-platform-line-sees-100m-game-downloads#VBqi9LDC5hsDSi8t.99|title=Asian messaging platform Line sees 100M game downloads|last=Loeb|first=Steven|date=March 14, 2013|access-date=May 14, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tango.me/2014/03/200-million-members/ |title=200 Million Members! – Tango – FREE voice, video, & text over 3G, 4G, & WiFi! |access-date=May 14, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140403213224/http://www.tango.me/2014/03/200-million-members/ |archive-date=April 3, 2014 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitaltrends.com/mobile/message-me-1-million-users/|title=MessageMe picks up 1 million users in 12 days, no thanks to Facebook |first=Francis |last=Bea |date=March 19, 2013 |access-date=May 14, 2013}}</ref><ref name="Dredge">{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/appsblog/2013/mar/08/best-iphone-ipad-apps-real-racing-3-marvel-unlimited |title=30 best iPhone and iPad apps this week |last=Dredge |first=Stuart |date=March 8, 2013 |work=The Guardian |access-date=May 14, 2013}}</ref> It was rated by [[PC Magazine|PCMag]] as "the simplest mobile chat application out there, with a good range of support."<ref name="Moscaritolo">{{cite web |url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2416345,00.asp |title=Video chat app tango hits 100m users, adds iPad support |last=Moscaritolo |first=Angela |date=March 7, 2013 |access-date=May 14, 2013}}</ref>

In 2017, Tango entered the live-streaming space, and has become a B2C platform for Live Video Broadcasts. Combining high-quality video streaming, a live messaging chat and a digital economy, Tango is a social community that allows content creators to share their talents and monetize their fans and followers.

Tango is available in many languages including Russian, Spanish, Turkish, Hindi and Vietnamese.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.techworld.com/picture-gallery/apps-wearables/best-free-software-for-video-calling-3685869/|title=Best free software for video calling|last=Williams|first=Hannah|website=Techworld|access-date=2019-10-07|archive-date=October 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007182707/https://www.techworld.com/picture-gallery/apps-wearables/best-free-software-for-video-calling-3685869/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Telegram===
[[Telegram (software)|Telegram]] provides the following features, as detailed below.<ref>[https://telegram.org/evolution The Evolution of Telegram], official website.</ref>

* Group threads: up to 200,000 members <ref>[https://telegram.org/faq#groups-and-channels Groups and Channels], official website FAQ.</ref> 
* Groups and channels: provides numerous official channels for various organizations. Has an internal search feature to enable searches to find various official outlets.

Telegram is a [[Cross-platform software|cross-platform]] [[Cloud computing|cloud]]-based [[instant messaging]], [[Videotelephony|video calling]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Video Calls and Seven Years of Telegram |url=https://telegram.org/blog/video-calls |website=Telegram company website |date=August 14, 2020 |access-date=15 August 2020}}</ref> and [[voice over IP|VoIP]] service. It was initially launched for iOS on 14 August 2013 in Russia, and is currently based in [[Dubai]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2013-08-30|title=Russia's Zuckerberg launches Telegram, a new instant messenger service|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUS74722569420130830|access-date=2020-11-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Meet Telegram, A Secure Messaging App From The Founders Of VK, Russia's Largest Social Network – TechCrunch|date=October 28, 2013 |url=https://techcrunch.com/2013/10/27/meet-telegram-a-secure-messaging-app-from-the-founders-of-vk-russias-largest-social-network/|access-date=2020-11-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title='Nobody can block it': how the Telegram app fuels global protest|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2020/nov/07/nobody-can-block-it-how-telegram-app-fuels-global-protest|access-date=2020-11-07|website=The Guardian|date=November 7, 2020}}</ref> Telegram [[Client–server model|client]] apps are available for [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[iOS]], [[Windows Phone]], [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]], [[macOS]] and [[Linux]], web interface is also available.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.telegram.org |title=Telegram Web |publisher=Web.telegram.org |date= |accessdate=2022-06-10}}</ref> As of April 2020, Telegram reached 400 million monthly active users.<ref name=":6">{{cite web|title=Telegram hits 400M monthly active users|url=https://techcrunch.com/2020/04/24/telegram-hits-400-million-monthly-active-users/|access-date=2020-11-03|website=TechCrunch|date=April 24, 2020|language=en-US|archive-date=July 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200717013304/https://techcrunch.com/2020/04/24/telegram-hits-400-million-monthly-active-users/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{cite web|date=2020-04-24|title=400 Million Users, 20,000 Stickers, Quizzes 2.0 and €400K for Creators of Educational Tests|url=https://telegram.org/blog/400-million|access-date=2020-10-30|website=Telegram}}</ref>

Telegram provides [[End-to-end encryption|end-to-end encrypted]] calls<ref>{{cite web|url=https://core.telegram.org/techfaq#q-how-are-voice-calls-authenticated|title=FAQ for the Technically Inclined|website=core.telegram.org|access-date=1 October 2017}}</ref> and optional end-to-end encrypted "secret" chats between two online users on smartphone clients, whereas cloud chats use client-server/ server-client encryption.  
Users can send text and voice messages, animated stickers, make voice and video calls, and share an unlimited number of images, documents(2GB per file), user locations, contacts, music, links etc.

Since March 2017, Telegram introduced its own [[voice call]]s. According to Telegram, there is a [[Artificial neural network|neural network]] working to learn various technical parameters about a call to provide better quality of the service for future uses. After a brief initial trial in Western Europe, voice calls are now available for use in most countries.<ref name="Telegram Voice Calls">{{Citation|url=https://telegram.org/blog/calls|publisher=Telegram|title=Voice Calls: Secure, Crystal-Clear, AI-Powered|date=30 March 2017|access-date=3 April 2017}}</ref>

Telegram announced in April 2020 that they would include group video calls by the end of the year.<ref name=":5"/> On 15 August 2020, Telegram added video calling with end-to-end encryption like Signal and WhatsApp, which Zoom does not have yet.<ref>{{cite web|last=O'Flaherty|first=Kate|title=Telegram Just Launched A Major New Feature To Beat Zoom|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/kateoflahertyuk/2020/08/16/telegram-just-launched-a-major-new-feature-to-beat-zoom/|access-date=2020-09-03|website=Forbes|language=en}}</ref> Currently offering one-to-one video calls, Telegram has plans to introduce secure group video calls later in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://telegram.org/blog/video-calls|title = Video Calls and Seven Years of Telegram|date = August 14, 2020}}</ref> Picture-in-picture mode is also available so that users have the option to simultaneously use the other functions of the app while still remaining on the call and are even able to turn their video off.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lyons|first=Kim|date=2020-08-15|title=Telegram launches one-on-one video calls on iOS and Android|url=https://www.theverge.com/2020/8/15/21370420/telegram-video-calls-os-android|access-date=2020-09-03|website=The Verge|language=en}}</ref>

Telegram's video and voice calls are secure and end-to-end encrypted.<ref>{{cite web|title=FAQ for the Technically Inclined|url=https://core.telegram.org/techfaq#q-how-are-voice-calls-authenticated|access-date=2020-10-30|website=core.telegram.org}}</ref>

===Viber===
Rakuten Viber, or simply [[Viber]], is a [[cross-platform]] [[voice over IP]] (VoIP) and [[instant messaging]] (IM) software application operated by Japanese multinational company [[Rakuten]], provided as [[freeware]] for the [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[iOS]], [[Microsoft Windows]], [[macOS]] and [[Linux]] platforms. Users are registered and identified through a [[cellular network|cellular telephone number]], although the service is accessible on desktop platforms without needing mobile connectivity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lifewire.com/viber-app-review-3426625|title=Viber App Review – Free Voice and Video Calls and Messaging|first=Nadeem |last=Unuth |website=Lifewire}}</ref> In addition to instant messaging it allows users to [[file transfer|exchange]] media such as images and video records, and also provides a paid international landline and mobile calling service called Viber Out.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lifewire.com/viber-out-review-3426597|title=Viber Out Review – How Good Is Viber for Paid Calling?|website=Lifewire}}</ref> As of 2018, there are over a billion registered users on the network.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/316414/viber-messenger-registered-users/|title=Viber: number of registered users 2018 |website=Statista}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.viber.com/about/|title=About Viber|website=Viber}}</ref>

WeChat provides text messaging, hold-to-talk voice messaging, broadcast (one-to-many) messaging, video conferencing, video games, sharing of photographs and videos, and location sharing.

WeChat provides text messaging, hold-to-talk voice messaging, [[broadcast]] (one-to-many) messaging, video calls and conferencing, video games, photograph and video sharing, as well as location sharing.<ref>{{YouTube|VAesMQ6VtK8|How China Is Changing Your Internet – The New York Times}} Published on 9 August 2016</ref> WeChat also allows users to exchange contacts with people nearby via [[Bluetooth]], as well as providing various features for contacting people at random if desired (if people are open to it). It can also integrate with other [[social networking service]]s such as [[Facebook]] and [[Tencent QQ]].<ref name="WeChat Welcome">{{cite web |url=http://help.wechat.com/cgi-bin/micromsg-bin/oshelpcenter?opcode=2&id=1703037JBzqu1703037vue22 |title=Welcome to WeChat |website=WeChat |access-date=12 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212193428/http://help.wechat.com/cgi-bin/micromsg-bin/oshelpcenter?opcode=2&id=1703037JBzqu1703037vue22 |archive-date=12 December 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> Photographs may also be embellished with [[Photographic filter|filters]] and captions, and [[machine translation|automatic translation]] service is available.

WeChat supports different instant messaging methods, including text message, voice message, walkie talkie, and stickers. Users can send previously saved or live pictures and videos, profiles of other users, coupons, lucky money packages, or current GPS locations with friends either individually or in a group chat. WeChat's character stickers, such as [[Tuzki]], resemble and compete with those of [[Line (software)|LINE]], a Japanese-South Korean messaging application.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.88-bar.com/2014/02/the-sticker-wars-wechats-creatives-go-up-against-line/|title=The Sticker Wars: WeChat's creatives go up against Line (updated)|date=5 February 2014|access-date=30 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170626083220/http://www.88-bar.com/2014/02/the-sticker-wars-wechats-creatives-go-up-against-line/|archive-date=26 June 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

WeChat users can register as a public account ({{lang|zh|公众号}}), which enables them to push feeds to subscribers, interact with subscribers and provide them with services. Users can also create an official account, which fall under service, subscription, or enterprise accounts. Once users as individuals or organizations set up a type of account, they cannot change it to another type. By the end of 2014, the number of WeChat official accounts had reached 8 million.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fang|first1=Yu (方雨)|script-title=zh:微信公众号已经进入标配期|url=http://www.bianews.com/news/41/n-440041.html|date=4 November 2014|access-date=10 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150312172849/http://www.bianews.com/news/41/n-440041.html|archive-date=12 March 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Official accounts of organizations can apply to be verified (cost 300 RMB or about US$45). Official accounts can be used as a platform for services such as hospital pre-registrations,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://politics.people.com.cn/n/2014/1125/c70731-26089420.html|script-title=zh:北京8家医院年内推出微信挂号服务 可挂专家号|work=people.com.cn|access-date=28 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402095635/http://politics.people.com.cn/n/2014/1125/c70731-26089420.html|archive-date=2 April 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> visa renewal<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tongyue.com/news/201501/88233.html|script-title=zh:港澳通行证续签新"技能"：微信续签送红包！|work=tongyue.com|access-date=28 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320153627/http://www.tongyue.com/news/201501/88233.html|archive-date=20 March 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> or credit card service.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cc.cmbchina.com/Common/Default.aspx?pageid=zxkf1|script-title=zh:信用卡智能"微客服"|access-date=30 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701190308/http://cc.cmbchina.com/Common/Default.aspx?pageid=zxkf1|archive-date=1 July 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> To create an official account, the applicant must register with Chinese authorities, which discourages "foreign companies".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Graziani |first1=Thomas |title=WeChat Official Account: a simple guide |url=https://walkthechat.com/wechat-official-account-simple-guide/ |website=Walkthechat |access-date=12 March 2020 |date=11 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200202090543/https://walkthechat.com/wechat-official-account-simple-guide/ |archive-date=2 February 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref>

{{Main|Moments (social networking)}}

"Moments" ({{lang|zh|朋友圈}}) is WeChat's brand name for its social feed of friends' updates. "Moments" is an interactive platform that allows users to post images, text, and short videos taken by users. It also allows users to share articles and music (associated with [[QQ Music]] or other web-based music services). Friends in the contact list can give thumbs up to the content and leave comments. Moments can be linked to Facebook and Twitter accounts, and can automatically post Moments content directly on these two platforms.<ref name="WeChat Welcome" />
 
In 2017 WeChat had a policy of a maximum of two advertisements per day per Moments user.<ref name=":5" />
